title: SB429 (2025 Regular): Relating to firearms; prescribing an effective date.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Oregon) (gun-policy Stage 5, Oregon); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Oregon text (Introduced, official copy, https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2025R1/Downloads/MeasureDocument/SB429/Introduced; sha256 58912c66c194bfefeec803c67524e4e54bd8e26216f018788b9725da6934cd51)
provenance.note: Introduced version (as filed). The first two quotes are the paragraphs under ORS 166.412 (3)(c) whose lead-in has struck words, so the lead-in is not quoted; the third is under (13)(b) (dealer immunity, whose lead-in also has struck words). The bill also tweaks wording around the permit-to-purchase and keeps the misdemeanor for transfers made without a permit or approval number (struck words in that subsection, not quoted). Takes effect the 91st day after sine die. No votes recorded.

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (ORS 166.412): (A) At least 72 hours have elapsed from the time at which the gun dealer requested the criminal background check; and
SECTION 1 (ORS 166.412): (B) The gun dealer has received a unique approval number from the department indicating that the purchaser is qualified to complete the transfer.
SECTION 1 (ORS 166.412): (C) Allows at least 72 hours to elapse between the request for the criminal background check and the transfer of the firearm or unfinished frame or receiver; and
SECTION 1 (ORS 166.412): (2)(a) The purchaser shall present to the gun dealer current identification meeting the requirements of subsection (4) of this section and a valid permit issued under ORS 166.505.
